description: Single-panel bright-field transmission electron micrograph of deformed Fe–30% Al, showing dislocation substructure. The field is dominated by dark, curved, kinked and partly straight dislocation segments threading a mottled, unevenly diffracting matrix; several near-parallel straight segments and elongated dipole-like loops are distinguishable, especially across the middle band and in the lower-left region. Broad, closely spaced background fringes traverse essentially the whole imaged area. In the lower right a solid black scale bar is labelled "0.2µm", and immediately above it a black arrow points up-and-to-the-right, marking the imaging vector; the caption states that vector is 1 1 0 and that the zone axis is near [0 0 1] (neither the indices nor any diffraction inset are printed on the image). No numeric data, axes or legend appear. Taken with Fig. 14–15, the panel supports the argument that in this weakly DO3-ordered Fe–30% Al alloy deformation leaves dislocation pairs formed by dislocation reactions, together with APBII residual-contrast fringes, rather than separated partials of glissile superdislocations.

observations.observation: The figure is a single bright-field TEM micrograph of a deformed alloy, with no sub-panel lettering, axes, legend or plotted data.
A solid black scale bar in the lower-right corner is labelled '0.2µm'.
A black arrow pointing up-and-to-the-right sits above the scale bar and marks the imaging vector; the Miller indices are not printed on the image.
Dark curved, kinked and locally straight dislocation segments are visible threading a mottled and unevenly diffracting matrix.
Broad, closely spaced background fringes run across essentially the entire imaged area.
The caption states the micrograph is of deformed Fe–30% Al, bright field, with the zone axis near [0 0 1] and the imaging vector (arrowed) 1 1 0.
The caption states the panel shows dislocation segments and background fringes.
The citing text states that the dislocation pairs observed in Figs. 14–16 are the result of dislocation reactions and do not correspond to the partials of the glissile superdislocations.

The citing text states the fringes traversing the area are due to residual contrast of APBII fringes produced during deformation of the weakly DO3-ordered material, because pairs of (1/2) 1 1 1 partials destroy this order during movement.

The citing text states deformation of Fe–Al with greater Al content occurs by movement of the same superdislocations composed of 2 × (1/2) 1 1 1 partial dislocations, with many straight near-screw dislocations, edge dipoles and loops.

The citing text states the APBI fault energy is sufficiently high in Fe–30% Al that partial separation within the superdislocation is small, so parallel image pairs correspond to short or long dipole dislocation pairs.
